title: A leading UTF-8 byte-order mark makes JSON file input fail to parse
outcome: A leading UTF-8 byte-order mark makes JSON file input fail to parse
acceptance: a JSON input file that begins with a single UTF-8 byte-order mark is accepted by every command that reads JSON from an @path file, with the same result as the same file without the mark
a test covers a marked and an unmarked file on both a bounded and an unbounded input path
the mark is removed only at the file input boundary: inline JSON, string contents and canonical bytes are unchanged, and a second leading mark is still refused
the raw byte limit is still enforced on the file bytes including the mark, and otherwise invalid JSON is still refused

completion.summary: Both @file JSON readers accept exactly one leading UTF-8 BOM. Raw bounded length includes the marker and is checked first; inline JSON and body/canonical meaning remain unchanged. Tests cover both readers, all core mutation call sites and policy input, malformed/double BOM/invalid UTF-8, exact limits and one-byte overflow. A limit-order mutation was killed and reverted. Full9 passed; wording corrections accepted by Fable2203 on freeze0563b3dd. Review had no functional defects; Claude exact pre-check was not executed because of its added echo suffix, while exact post-check passed. No Git/install; shipped update remains due at installation.
